nodes.content: Investigate contact-rich insertion policies that distinguish recoverable misalignment from jamming under visual occlusion and unknown friction.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% insertion success on held-out peg geometries and friction conditions with 0.2 mm clearance.
Keep peak contact force below 20 N in ≥99% of trials, including jam recovery.

nodes.content: Use geometry-conditioned, friction-adaptive wrench-history beliefs to distinguish misalignment from jamming under occlusion and select 18 N-capped probing or retreat.
Can 0.1 mm, 18 N-capped lateral probes distinguish recoverable offsets from wedging by wrench history under occlusion and unknown friction?
Under occlusion, wrench histories from 0.1 mm, 18 N-capped probes achieve jam-versus-offset AUROC ≥0.90 across unseen geometries and friction.
Collect occluded probe wrench traces across friction and geometry splits; label jams versus offsets; evaluate classifier AUROC and peak force.
Run OccludedProbe-0.2: collect labeled occluded 0.1 mm, 18 N-capped probe traces; score jam-offset AUROC and peak force on held-out geometries/frictions.
On OccludedProbe-0.2, held-out geometry/friction jam-offset AUROC reached 0.93; 99.3% of probes stayed below 20 N.
Advance the classifier to guarded insertion trials, given 0.93 held-out AUROC and 99.3% probe-force compliance.
OccludedProbe-0.2 dataset and evaluation report contain labeled wrench traces, held-out geometry/friction splits, jam-offset AUROC, and probe-force distributions.
Using OccludedProbe-0.2 held-out splits, run 1,000 0.2 mm-clearance insertions with belief-guided probes and retreat; record success and recovery peak force.
Across 1,000 held-out 0.2 mm-clearance insertions, success was 87.4%; only 97.8% kept peak recovery force below 20 N.
Does belief-guided insertion meet both success and peak-force targets during jam recovery on held-out geometries and friction conditions?
Fuse fingertip shear with wrist wrench to estimate friction online; apply 16 N barrier-controlled axial unload before lateral correction.
Calibrate shear-based friction estimates, train barrier-controlled unload-and-realign, then test 1,000 held-out occluded insertions against both targets.
Using OccludedProbe-0.2 splits, collect synchronized fingertip-shear and wrist-wrench traces; train friction estimation and 16 N barrier-controlled realignment.
ShearGuard-v1 pairs a calibrated friction estimator with a 16 N barrier-controlled unload-and-realign policy and synchronized shear–wrench training traces.
Run 1,000 paired occluded 0.2-mm-clearance insertions across held-out geometries/frictions; compare ShearGuard-v1 against wrench-only baseline on success and recovery peak force.
Across 1,000 held-out insertions, ShearGuard-v1 achieved 92.1% success; 99.4% kept peak contact force below 20 N, including recovery.
Are ShearGuard-v1’s six >20 N excursions caused by friction-estimator lag during stick–slip recovery?
Reducing friction-estimator latency below 10 ms will cut >20 N stick–slip recovery excursions from six to ≤1 per 1,000 trials.
Compare 1,000 paired held-out insertions using <10 ms versus baseline ShearGuard-v1 friction updates; record success and >20 N recovery excursions.
In 1,000 held-out paired trials, <10 ms updates cut >20 N recovery excursions from six to one; success reached 92.2%.
Select <10 ms ShearGuard-v1 over wrench-only insertion: 92.2% versus 87.4% success and 99.9% versus 97.8% force compliance.
Infer jams from tactile pressure maps; use chance-constrained impedance MPC for geometry-adaptive recovery under a 17 N force budget.
Can tactile pressure asymmetry identify jams earlier than shear–wrench estimates during high-friction, occluded insertions?
In high-friction occluded trials, tactile pressure asymmetry detects jams ≥20 ms earlier than ShearGuard-v1 at ≥95% precision.
Collect 300 high-friction occluded pressure-map trials alongside ShearGuard-v1; compare jam-detection lead time at matched ≥95% precision.
Across 300 high-friction trials, pressure asymmetry led ShearGuard-v1 by 8 ms at 95% precision, below the hypothesized 20 ms.
Using ShearGuard-v1 as comparator, test pressure-map jam lead time at ≥95% precision on 400 unseen-geometry, high-friction insertions.
On 400 unseen-geometry high-friction insertions, pressure maps detected jams 24 ms earlier than ShearGuard-v1 at 96% precision.
Limit pressure-map integration to unseen-geometry, high-friction cases; 24 ms lead there contrasts with 8 ms in the initial trial.
Fuse contact acoustics with proprioceptive slip estimates; trigger 16 N-capped retract-and-rotate recovery when jam probability exceeds 0.8.
Collect audio–slip traces; train 0.8-threshold recovery; test success and peak force on 1,000 held-out geometry/friction, 0.2-mm-clearance insertions.
Augment ShearGuard-v1 with synchronized contact audio and proprioceptive slip; train 0.8-threshold, 16 N-capped retract-and-rotate recovery.
AudioSlip-v1 adds synchronized contact-audio/slip features and a 0.8-jam-probability trigger for 16 N-capped retract-and-rotate recovery.
Compare AudioSlip-v1 against ShearGuard-v1 in 1,000 occluded, held-out geometry/friction 0.2-mm-clearance insertions; measure success and recovery peak force.
Across 1,000 held-out insertions, AudioSlip-v1 achieved 94.0% success versus ShearGuard-v1’s 92.2%; 99.8% stayed below 20 N, including recovery.
Adopt AudioSlip-v1: success rose from 92.2% to 94.0%, while 99.8% force compliance remained above target.
Use 0.05° torsional micro-dithers to distinguish wedging from frictional sticking, then switch to 15 N-capped compliant retreat.
Can 0.05° torsional micro-dithers distinguish geometric wedging from frictional sticking without exceeding 20 N on unseen pegs?
At 0.05°, dither torque–displacement hysteresis classifies wedging versus sticking with AUROC ≥0.90 and ≥99% sub-20 N force compliance.
Collect labeled 0.05° dither hysteresis on training pegs; evaluate wedging–sticking AUROC and peak-force compliance on unseen geometries/frictions.
Integrate 0.05° dithers and 15 N-capped retreat into AudioSlip-v1; measure wedging–sticking AUROC, insertion success, and peak force on unseen pegs.
Dither AUROC reached 0.92 and 99.5% stayed below 20 N; insertion success fell to 88.6% versus AudioSlip-v1’s 94.0%.
Evaluate AudioSlip-v1 plus 0.05° dithers on 400 high-friction unseen pegs; label wedging/sticking and record AUROC, success, and peak force.
On 400 high-friction unseen pegs, dither hysteresis achieved 0.84 wedging–sticking AUROC, below the hypothesized 0.90.
Reject torsional dithers for deployment: success dropped to 88.6%, and high-friction wedging–sticking AUROC was only 0.84.
For moderate friction (μ≤0.4), 0.05° dither hysteresis achieves wedging–sticking AUROC ≥0.90 and ≥99% sub-20 N compliance on unseen pegs.
Test labeled 0.05° dither traces on unseen pegs at μ≤0.4; measure wedging–sticking AUROC and sub-20 N compliance.
Reassess rejected dithers using AudioSlip-v1 on μ≤0.4 unseen pegs; measure wedging–sticking AUROC, insertion success, and sub-20 N compliance.
On 400 μ≤0.4 unseen pegs, dither AUROC reached 0.93 with 99.5% sub-20 N compliance, but insertion success was 88%.
Retain dithers only as an offline moderate-friction diagnostic; 0.93 AUROC does not offset 88% insertion success.
